boundary.message: You came that way once. It is the only part of tonight that is over.

content.outro: The bell had one thing left to say, and the last hand on the rope was yours.
content.premise: You wake face-down on the Barrow Flat at the first ebb of the night, a lead passage-token closed in your fist and nothing behind you but water. Above you Halgrave steps up out of the sand: a shore of graves, a cut road on a sea cliff, a gatehouse, an outer ward that has been under the tide for fifty-one years, a roofless cloister, a hall with its roof still on, a cistern cut into the rock, and at the crown a plain square tower with a hole of sky at its top. The bell in that hole is named Mercy. It has had no tongue since the night it was made to lie, and its tongue has lain under the water of the cistern well ever since. For about two hours tonight, the sea will be low enough to give it back. Everyone still on this rock wants the bell rung, or wants it never rung again, and no two of them mean the same thing by it.
content.theme: A fortified priory on a tidal crag off a drowned coast, fifty-one years after its bell rang the wrong number and the sea took the people who believed it. One night of two ebbs, and the second is the lowest water in living memory.
content.title: The Drowned Bell
